answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral to each identity and recording equivocation across a shared horizon. When k coordinated identities sign conflicting histories, pairwise evidence creates O(k²) penalty exposure; detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, so adding identities amplifies rather than diversifies risk. The resulting plume of correlated faults is harder to disguise, while honest operators retain an oasis of safety through independent, consistent behavior.
